steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package to enable component state management.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have the necessary imports to create a React component with state management capabilities.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components with state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are not correct. Please import React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main DeploymentStrategies component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named DeploymentStrategies that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a component using either function declaration or arrow function syntax. Make sure it returns null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the DeploymentStrategies component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A component named DeploymentStrategies is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The DeploymentStrategies component is created and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main component that will serve as the container for our deployment strategies lesson.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the component is named exactly 'DeploymentStrategies' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you've defined a component named 'DeploymentStrategies' that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize state for selected strategy
steps.instruction: Inside your DeploymentStrategies component, initialize a state variable called 'selectedStrategy' with useState, setting its default value to an empty string.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The syntax is: const [selectedStrategy, setSelectedStrategy] = useState('');
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state initialization for a selected option
const [selectedOption, setSelectedOption] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'selectedStrategy' initialized to track which deployment strategy is currently selected.
successCriteria: The state variable 'selectedStrategy' is declared with useState and initialized to an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state to track the selected deployment strategy.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with the variable name 'selectedStrategy' and initializing it to an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Use useState to create a 'selectedStrategy' state variable with an empty string as default value.

steps.title: Define strategy selection handler
steps.instruction: Inside your DeploymentStrategies component, define a function named handleStrategySelect that takes a strategyName parameter and updates the selectedStrategy state with it.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses the setSelectedStrategy state setter to update the state with the provided strategy name.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a handler function that can be called to update the selected deployment strategy in state.
successCriteria: The component contains a function named handleStrategySelect that takes a parameter and calls setSelectedStrategy with that parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a handler function that will update the state when a deployment strategy is selected.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function takes a parameter and calls setSelectedStrategy with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function named handleStrategySelect that updates the selectedStrategy state with the provided strategy name.

steps.title: Create the main container structure
steps.instruction: In your DeploymentStrategies component, return a div container with a main heading 'Deployment Strategies' and a brief introductory paragraph explaining deployment strategies.
steps.hint: Replace the current return null with a div containing an h1 and a p element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a structured container with a heading and introductory paragraph about deployment strategies.
successCriteria: The component returns a div containing an h1 with text 'Deployment Strategies' and a p element with introductory text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main container structure with a heading and introductory paragraph.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your div contains both an h1 with 'Deployment Strategies' and a paragraph with introductory text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div container with an h1 and p element. Check that you've replaced 'return null' with the appropriate JSX structure.

steps.title: Add strategy selection buttons
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a div container with buttons for each deployment strategy: 'Blue-Green', 'Canary', 'Rolling Update', and 'Recreate'. Wire each button's onClick to call handleStrategySelect with the corresponding strategy name.
steps.hint: Create a div element containing four button elements. Each button should have an onClick handler that calls handleStrategySelect with the appropriate strategy string.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: Adding interactive buttons
steps.expectedOutcome: A div container with four buttons appears in the component's return statement, each wired to call handleStrategySelect with its respective strategy name.
successCriteria: The component returns a div containing four buttons with labels 'Blue-Green', 'Canary', 'Rolling Update', and 'Recreate', each with an onClick handler calling handleStrategySelect with the correct strategy string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the strategy selection buttons with proper click handlers.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure all four buttons are present and each onClick correctly calls handleStrategySelect with the matching strategy name.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a div with four buttons, each with the correct label and onClick handler that calls handleStrategySelect with the strategy string.

steps.title: Display the selected strategy
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a conditional display section that shows the currently selected strategy name when one is selected, otherwise show a prompt to select a strategy.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator to conditionally render content based on the selectedStrategy state value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show either the selected deployment strategy name or a prompt to select one, depending on whether a strategy has been chosen.
successCriteria: A conditional display section is added that shows the selected strategy name when selectedStrategy has a value, otherwise shows a prompt message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering to display the selected deployment strategy or a prompt.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your conditional section properly checks the selectedStrategy state value and displays appropriate content for both cases.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional display section is missing or doesn't properly handle both cases (selected strategy and prompt). Review how to use ternary operators for conditional rendering.

steps.title: Add strategy description section
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a section that displays detailed descriptions for each deployment strategy based on the selectedStrategy state. Use conditional rendering to show different descriptions.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator or switch statement to conditionally render different description text based on selectedStrategy.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will include a section that shows educational descriptions for different deployment strategies when selected.
successCriteria: A description section is added with conditional rendering based on selectedStrategy, showing different text for at least two strategies.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a strategy description section with conditional rendering.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a description section, but make sure it conditionally renders different text based on selectedStrategy.
steps.feedbackWrong: The description section is missing or doesn't properly conditionally render based on selectedStrategy.

steps.title: Add visual indicators for strategy status
steps.instruction: Add a conditional className to each strategy button that applies a visual style when that strategy matches the selectedStrategy state.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator to check if the button's strategy matches selectedStrategy, and apply a CSS class like 'active' when true.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: conditional styling for active item
<button className={activeItem === 'item1' ? 'active' : ''}>Item 1</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each strategy button will have visual feedback (like a colored border or background) when selected, making the active strategy clear to users.
successCriteria: Each button has a conditional className attribute
The className changes based on selectedStrategy state
Visual feedback is applied to the active strategy button
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added visual indicators to show which deployment strategy is currently selected.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure each button's className changes conditionally based on the selectedStrategy state.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a className attribute to each button that changes when that strategy is selected. Use a ternary operator to compare with selectedStrategy.

steps.title: Add deployment simulation controls
steps.instruction: Add a 'Simulate Deployment' button that, when clicked, logs a simulation message to the console for the currently selected strategy.
steps.hint: Add a button element with an onClick handler that calls a function to log the simulation details.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: button that triggers an action
<button onClick={() => console.log('Action triggered')}>
  Trigger Action
</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'Simulate Deployment' button appears below the existing content. When clicked, it logs a message to the console showing which deployment strategy is being simulated.
successCriteria: The 'Simulate Deployment' button is added with an onClick handler that logs a simulation message for the selected strategy.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the simulation button. This completes the basic deployment strategies interface with interactive simulation capability.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has an onClick handler that logs a message about the selected strategy.
steps.feedbackWrong: The simulation button isn't working correctly. Check that you've added a button with an onClick handler that logs the selected strategy.
